City of Encinitas
City Council - 6:00 p.m.
AGENDA
WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 19, 2014 -
06:00 PM
p.m.
City of Encinitas - City Council Chambers
505 S. Vulcan Avenue
Encinitas, California 92024
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
2.
ROLL CALL
3.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
4.
SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS AND PROCLAMATIONS
4A.
Presentation of Proclamation to the Leucadia 101 Main Street Association proclaiming November 29, 2014 as Small Business Saturday
4B.
Sister City Delegates
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a "WHITE" speaker slip to the City Clerk. If at least two (2) Council Members agree, direction may be given to staff to put an item on a future agenda or provide additional information to answer a question.
6.
REPORT FROM CLOSED SESSION (IF HELD)
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a "PINK" speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar. The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
8A.
Approval of the Minutes of the 10/22/14 Regular Meeting. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Approve the Minutes.
2014-11-19 Item 8A - Minutes
8B.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants List.
2014-11-19 Item 8B - Warrants
8C.
Award of contract for the grounds and landscape maintenance services - service area one. Contact Person: Park and Beach Superintendent Frenken
Award of contract for Grounds and Landscape Maintenance Services for Service Area One to Excel Landscape in the amount of $291,600.
2014-11-19 Item 8C - Contract Award for Grounds Landscape
8D.
Introduction of Ordinance 2014-12 amending Encinitas Municipal Code. Contact Person: Administrative Support Coordinator Morrow
Introduce Ordinance 2014-12 entitled, "An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas, California, Amending Encinitas Municipal Code Chapters 2.28 Cabinet Team Positions and Officers; 2.40 Traffic and Public Safety Commission; 14.08 Traffic Administration; 14.41 Permit Parking Zones; 15.04 Construction on Public Rights-of-Way; 18.08 Sewer Connection Fees; 23.24 Grading Erosion and Sediment Control; 23.36 Right-of-Way Standards, Street Improvement Standards, and Building Line Requirements; 23.40 Floodplain Management Regulations; 30.48 Accessory Use Regulations."
2014-11-19 Item 8D - Ordinance 2014-12 PW Engineering Organizational Changes
8E.
Consideration of Resolution 2014-64 approving Amendment to the Encina Wastewater Authority Revised Basic Agreement. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Wilson
Adopt Resolution 2014-64 approving Amendment to the Encina Wastewater Authority Revised Basic Agreement.
2014-11-19 Item 8E - Res 2014-64 Encina Wastewater Authority Revised Basic Agreement
8F.
Consideration of Resolution 2014-65 Supporting the Redesignation of North San Diego County as a Recycling Market Development Zone Due to an Increase in Boundaries and Adoption of a Negative Declaration Addendum. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Wilson
Adopt Resolution 2014-65 Supporting the Redesignation of North San Diego County as a Recycling Market Development Zone Due to an Increase in Boundaries and Adoption of a Negative Declaration Addendum.
2014-11-19 Item 8F - Resolution 2014-65 Supporting Redesignation
8G.
Amendment to the agreement with Tyler Technologies, Inc. for the purchase and implementation of Energov Software for business registration and City Clerk permits. Contact Person: Project Manager Van Pelt
1) Authorize the City Manager to enter into an amended agreement with Tyler Technologies, Inc. for professional services and software licenses in an amount of $294,249; 2) Authorize estimated hardware costs of $122,632; and 3) Approve a 15% contingency amount of $62,532.
2014-11-19 Item 8G - Amendment to Tyler Technologies, Inc. Contract for Energov
8H.
Authorize the Director of Public Works, or his designee to execute Contract Amendment No. 1 with RBF to prepare an Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for the North Coast Highway 101 Streetscape Project (CS04D). Contact Person: Associate City Engineer Villa
1) Authorize the Director of Public Works, or his designee, to execute a contract amendment with RBF for the North Coast Highway 101 Streetscape project to prepare an Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for a fee not to exceed $129,180, including 10% contingency; and 2) Authorize overall contract expenditures with RBF for the design phase of work not to exceed $888,512.
2014-11-19 Item 8H - RBF Contract Amendment for N. Coast Hwy 101 Streetscape
8I.
Consideration and approval of draft City Council Policy C029, commonly referred to as the Invasive Plant Policy, as directed by the City Council on July 16, 2014. Contact Person: Associate Planner Winter
Consider and approve draft City Council Policy C029.
2014-11-19 Item 8I - Invasive Plant Policy
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
10A.
Consideration of possible options to amend the City's Affordable Unit Policy in an effort to incentivize participation; consideration of possible options to address the expiration date currently set for units permitted under the City's Housing Certification Program; and, consideration of options for a public mailer that will be sent to residents in an effort to gauge interest in program participation. Contact Person: Principal Planner Langager
Discuss and consider available options, along with associated benefits and drawbacks, to revise the Affordable Unit Policy, Housing Certification Program and public mailer and provide staff direction, as deemed appropriate.
2014-11-19 Item 10A - City Affordable Unit Policy
10B.
Public hearing and adoption of Resolution 2014-58 regarding findings related to the unexpended fund balance for impact/mitigation fees collected prior to 6/30/09 and acceptance of the annual report of development/mitigation fees for fiscal year ended June 30, 2014 as required by the California Mitigation Fee Act. Contact Person: Finance Manager Shoemaker
Adopt Resolution 2014-58 regarding findings related to the unexpended fund balance for fees collected prior to 6/30/09 and accept the annual report of development impact/mitigation fees for fiscal year ended June 30, 2014.
2014-11-19 Item 10B - Findings & 5-Year Report for Mitigation Impact Fees
10C.
Report on the Financial Results for Fiscal Year 2013-14. Contact Person: Finance Manager Shoemaker
Receive and file report. Approve and adopt the actual ending fund balances for FY2013-14 as beginning fund balances for FY2014-15. Approve the revised Schedule A for FY2014-15 presented in Attachment 5. Direct staff to include as part of each annual budget process City Council consideration of making a payment towards the City's unfunded pension liability from the prior year budget surplus.
2014-11-19 Item 10C - Financial Results for Fiscal Year 2013-14
10D.
Quarterly Update on Financial Condition: First Quarter Fiscal Year 2014-15. Contact Person: Finance Manager Shoemaker
Adopt Resolution 2014-59 approving the First Quarter Budget Adjustments for FY2014-15.
2014-11-19 Item 10D - Quarterly Update on Financial Condition- First Quarter Fiscal Year 2014-15
11.
INFORMATIONAL ITEMS
12.
COUNCIL MEMBER INITIATED AGENDA ITEM There are no Council Member initiated Items.
13.
FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS ADDED BY COUNCIL MEMBERS
14.
CITY COUNCIL MEMBER REPORTS PURSUANT TO AB1234 (GC 53232.3(d)) / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF
15.
CITY MANAGER REPORTS / PENDING FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
2014-11-19 Item 15 - City Manager Follow Up Log
16.
CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS
17.
ADJOURNMENT
Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
